source_title: WHO household air pollution and health
direct_observation: 2.1 billion people cook with polluting fuels or inefficient stoves; women and children bear disproportionate exposure and health burden
closed_stage: global burden health mechanism and gendered exposure
missing_stage: named household exposure sustained use affordability health and agency
next_test: measure personal exposure repeated use affordability and health by household member

source_title: WHO 2025 household air pollution technical brief
direct_observation: brief identifies barriers and calls for granular household-energy data including time fuel collection and health implications
missing_stage: exclusive versus stacked use and lived outcomes
next_test: add survey fields for parallel stoves cooking time fuel collection and exposure

direct_observation: clean-cooking access rose from 64 percent in 2015 to 74 percent in 2023 but about 2.1 billion remain dependent on polluting fuels
missing_stage: affordability reliability supply persistence and outcome
next_test: disaggregate rural poor remote and displaced households and follow refill continuity

source_title: Clean cooking in IEA Africa Energy Outlook
direct_observation: clean cooking is a major prosperity challenge and lack of access affects roughly four in five sub-Saharan African households with time and fuel burdens
closed_stage: regional scale investment and development mechanism
missing_stage: named user uptake repeated use exposure gender agency and market durability
next_test: compare urban and rural fuel/appliance routes with cost reliability and use logs

source_title: UN Women Gender and Environment Survey Cambodia
direct_observation: women remain overwhelmingly responsible for cooking in both clean and unclean-fuel households and fuel-collection roles vary
missing_stage: agency bargaining power time use safety and decision authority
next_test: measure who cooks collects pays decides maintains and benefits before and after intervention
